clusters.headline_hint: Tensions mount over potential fresh US-Israel strikes on Iran as crude oil prices surge past $117

claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated at a South Florida rally on Friday that US warships returning from the war with Iran could stop near Cuba before Secretary of State Marco Rubio negotiates a deal.
The United States imposed further sanctions on the Cuban government after expressing dissatisfaction with recent bilateral discussions.
Cuba has been struggling with a severe economic and energy crisis since 2020.
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States may launch 'another little Epic Fury' attack on Iran.
The joint Israeli-American military operation named Epic Fury launched at the end of February sparked the war with Iran.
Foreign ministers from eight European and Middle Eastern countries gathered at a summit in Istanbul to urge the US and Israel not to renew military attacks on Iran.
Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia formed the Mecca defensive security pact in August.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that military intervention in Iran is not a solution and warned that new attacks would spread conflict across the region.
A person briefed on US and Israeli war planning told NPR that both countries were preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran after the US midterm elections.
A federal magistrate judge ruled that Donald Trump must sit for a deposition in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC.
Almost 21 million Americans have already cast their ballots in the US midterm elections through mail-in or early in-person voting.
The US midterm elections are scheduled for November 3, while Israel's election takes place on October 27.
Two US aircraft carrier strike groups are currently located in the Arabian Sea, with a third expected to arrive by late November.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on social media that any participation or cooperation by regional states in a US or Israeli operation would face a decisive response.

clusters.headline_hint: Israel launches West Bank military operation and orders lockdown following deadly Hebron attack

claims.text: The Israel Defence Forces launched a targeted counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a shooting.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Hebron and ordered a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank following an attack that wounded five people.
The Israeli military reported that two attackers involved in the Hebron shooting were killed by security forces.
Israel imposed a lockdown across the occupied West Bank after a shooting near Hebron killed two Israeli soldiers.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich posted a video showing a bulldozer tearing down a Palestinian home near the site of the Hebron firefight.
Israel's High Court issued a temporary order halting home demolitions in Hebron following an urgent petition filed by a human rights lawyer.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that clan neighbourhoods in Hebron from which attackers emerged would be evacuated of their residents.
More than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed in the occupied West Bank by Israeli forces or settlers since October 7, 2023.
Emergency responders reported five people were injured, some critically, during a shooting attack near the Yehuda Junction outside Hebron.
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stated that the attack demonstrates a need to restrict Palestinian freedom of movement in the West Bank.

clusters.headline_hint: Gunmen open fire during church funeral in Karak, Jordan, killing seven people

claims.text: Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya stated that a horrific terrorist act was carried out against a church by a group of extremists.
Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning starting Friday following the Karak church attack.
At least seven people were killed and 34 wounded when two masked gunmen opened fire at a church in Karak, Jordan.
Unidentified gunmen opened fire during a funeral procession at a church in Hmoud, located in Jordan's Karak governorate.
Witness Khalid al-Mdanat told BBC Arabic that the attack inside the church lasted approximately 15 minutes before the gunmen fled in a pickup truck.
King Abdullah II of Jordan declared on social media that the country would confront the terrorist act in Karak with the harshest penalties.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the church shooting in Jordan as a heinous terrorist attack that violated religious and humanitarian values.
Jordan's Director of Public Security Major General Obeidallah Maaytah reported that 27 people wounded in the shooting remained hospitalized.
Grand Imam of Al-Azhar Ahmed al-Tayeb expressed condolences to the families of victims and condemned the shooting as a heinous terrorist attack.
In 2016, a series of deadly attacks by gunmen in Karak killed 10 people, including seven police officers.

clusters.headline_hint: Emmanuel Macron condemns 'racist terror attack' after drive-by shooting near Paris leaves one dead

claims.text: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned a drive-by shooting spree in Trappes and La Verrière as a premeditated racist terror attack.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nu!1ez stated that a gunman opened fire across three separate locations over a 15-minute span west of Paris.
One person was killed and at least five others were injured, including a 12-year-old girl, in the drive-by shooting spree.
French authorities identified the suspect as 39-year-old Kévin T, who had four previous convictions that were automatically expunged under French law.
Police found a Sten-type submachine gun in the suspect's car and discovered three gas cylinders connected to an electric timer in his apartment.
The mixed martial arts academy Atch Academy identified the young man killed in the shooting as Pengo Bossio Wangi.
Trappes Mayor Ali Rabeh described the shooting as objectively a racist attack that was probably motivated by Islamophobia.
La Verrière Mayor Nicolas Dainville stated that two of the wounded victims in his town were school cleaners of African origin.
The mother of the injured 12-year-old girl told RTL that her daughter was wearing a headscarf when she was shot eight times.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on social media that all resources of the security forces and judiciary are fully mobilized.

clusters.headline_hint: Russia and Ukraine agree to localized ceasefire in Oleshky

claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated that First Lady Melania Trump's initiative led to a localized ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky.
The White House announced that First Lady Melania Trump helped broker a localized ceasefire in Oleshky to enable humanitarian aid entry and civilian evacuations.
First Lady Melania Trump arranged for conservative news outlet Newsmax to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams during the mission in Oleshky.
Ukrainian and Russian forces agreed to stop firing in Oleshky starting at 02:00 GMT on October 27, 2026.
Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia confirmed that an operation to unblock Oleshky and assist residents would begin following the ceasefire announcement.
Oleshky had a pre-war population of 24,000 residents before Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Ukrainian officials estimate that around 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas.
Around 34 children have been returned between Russia and Ukraine since 2025 through diplomatic channels involving representatives of Melania Trump.
Approximately 90 percent of Oleshky's territory was flooded following the collapse of the Kakhovka Dam in 2023.

clusters.headline_hint: Critical vulnerabilities in PHP programming language trigger global cybersecurity warnings

claims.text: Cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif discovered two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language in August.
Cybersecurity firm Wiz estimated that the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities affected around 70 percent of all websites worldwide.
PHP released a security advisory on October 23 urging users to temporarily disable the session upload progress feature to mitigate a remote code execution risk.
Cybersecurity firm Censys detected approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services running potentially vulnerable versions of PHP in an October 22 snapshot.
Qualys identified 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organizations, with 73 percent deployed on internet-facing assets.
The US National Security Agency issued an advisory urging organizations using PHP to immediately apply patches to prevent unauthorized server access.
Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince reported that attempt counts to exploit the PHP flaws jumped from tens of thousands shortly after disclosure to millions.
An unauthorized leak on Hacker News forced PHP developers to release emergency security patches on October 21 ahead of schedule.
Multiple European government websites and the Port of Rotterdam temporarily took services offline following the disclosure of the PHP flaws.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi issued an urgent request for entities to apply PHP patches or temporarily suspend websites to minimize cyber risk.

clusters.headline_hint: Protests and political row escalate across India over Special Intensive Revision of voter lists

claims.text: The Disha Students' Organisation and Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra organised a protest outside Mumbai University's Kalina campus on October 23, 2026.

Protesters outside Mumbai University demanded the complete withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and fresh elections using previous voter lists.
Protesters outside Mumbai University called for the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of Election Commissioners.
Dr. Pooja, coordinator of Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra, alleged that the Special Intensive Revision exercise could disenfranchise Muslims, Dalits, Adivasis, and working-class voters.
On May 27, 2026, the Supreme Court of India upheld the validity of the Special Intensive Revision exercise conducted in Bihar.

Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote separate letters to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29 objecting to a revised work allocation order issued by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg.

The Cabinet Secretariat declined to intervene in the Election Commissioners' complaint, stating that the letters were sent in an individual capacity rather than as a formal communication from the Election Commission as a whole.
Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg issued the work reallocation order while filling in for Deputy Election Commissioner (Administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while Yeturu was on leave.
The work reallocation order issued by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg was never implemented following objections from Election Commissioners.
Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu is a former Uttarakhand chief secretary who holds an MBBS, a Master of Arts in History, and a law degree.
Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi is a former Haryana chief secretary and former Union Personnel Secretary who holds a PhD in International Economics.
A Cabinet note prepared on August 3, 2026, initially proposed seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's opinion regarding the Election Commissioners' complaint against Maneesh Garg.
The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition by student leader Neha Bora challenging a notice from a special executive magistrate directing her to furnish a bond to maintain peace.

Neha Bora, president of the All India Students' Association, was detained on October 16, 2026, during a protest near Barakhamba Road demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The special executive magistrate's notice directed Neha Bora to furnish a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with a surety.
Protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the special intensive revision of electoral rolls have taken place in Delhi and across India since October 2.

clusters.headline_hint: India blames Chinese patrolling deviations for disturbing border peace along LAC

claims.text: Indo-Tibetan Border Police Director General Shatrujeet Kapur stated publicly that Indian and Chinese troops have been engaged in ongoing face-offs at several locations along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh.
Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that the border situation gets disturbed when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.
The Ministry of Home Affairs allocated Rs 400 crore for the modernisation of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, with 70% earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities.
Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera called on the Indian government to send an all-party delegation to Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh to verify whether Chinese forces have encroached on Indian territory.
Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera stated that India's trade deficit with China has ballooned to $113 billion.
Tensions and several face-offs occurred between Indian and Chinese troops near Taksing in Upper Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh during July and August.
India and China held their first round of military commanders' talks in the eastern sector in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and 7.
Chinese President Xi Jinping advocated for a dual-track approach to bilateral relations and border issues during his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police guards the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control between India and China.
In July, Chinese PLA troops pitched tents approximately 6 to 7 kilometers inside India's perception of the Line of Actual Control near Maja after an initial confrontation.
China claims a large portion of Arunachal Pradesh as 'South Tibet' and officially refers to the state as Zangnan.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police posted video footage of DG Shatrujeet Kapur's speech on social media on Thursday night before later deleting it.
